title: Speaking practice (hard): Natural history museum guide and keeping in touch
author: toefl-claude-test-generator
description: Listen and repeat with a natural history museum supervisor (long sentences packed with articles, passives, present and past perfect and relative clauses); an interview on technology and keeping in touch that requires past narration, comparing, weighing a trade-off and predicting.

tasks.setting: You are training as a volunteer guide at a natural history museum. Listen to the volunteer supervisor and repeat exactly what you hear.

items.text: Visitors can't touch the fossils in the main hall.
The dinosaur skeleton in the entrance was found by a farmer in the nineteen thirties.
If a school group arrives early, you should take the children to the cloakroom before the tour begins.
The insect collection, which has been closed since the spring, will reopen once the new cases have been installed.
Most of the guides who've worked here for a few years say the questions children ask are the hardest.
The meteorite that had been stored in the basement for decades turned out to be older than the experts expected.

tasks.intro: Hello, and thanks for taking part. I'm interviewing people about how technology affects the way we communicate with friends and family.

questions.text: To begin, how do you usually stay in contact with the people who are important to you, and how often do you talk to them?
Tell me about a time when a message, a call or a video chat made a real difference to you or to someone you know. What happened?
Some people say that sending short messages every day keeps friendships stronger than meeting in person once a month. Compare the two, and explain which you think matters more.
Many schools now ban mobile phones during the school day. Do you think this is a good policy, and how might it change the way young people communicate in the future?
